Adaptation and low-emissions strategies remain plannedThe NDC says the national adaptation plan and long-term low-emissions strategy are to be completed, consulted on and approved, with international cooperation intended to improve access to climate-action finance.Planned action+2 points1 document2 quotes

The document says Belarus plans to finalize, consult broadly on, and approve a national climate adaptation action plan through 2040 and a national long-term low-greenhouse-gas-emissions development strategy through 2050. It also plans international cooperation to study good practice and strengthen access to financing mechanisms for mitigation and adaptation, including emissions trading and green bonds; these are plans, not statements that the mechanisms or strategies are already implemented.

    The NDCs identify national laws and other regulatory acts as governing climate change. Analysis notes

No distinct climate loss-and-damage statement was found in either document’s retrieved findings. The later NDC reports hazards and economic damage as climate impacts, not as a distinct loss-and-damage issue.

Document comparison & edition notes

By document

  • BEL-NDC2 The earlier NDC describes policy governance and programmes, 2030 emissions targets, climate-risk work, reporting and inventory methods, LULUCF treatment, and research inputs. It also reports constraints on low-carbon investment and an intention to raise future ambition.
  • BEL-NDC1 The later NDC sets 2035 unconditional and conditional emissions targets, reports climate governance, support needs, adaptation planning, reporting and research activities, and land-sector sink information. It does not contain a distinct loss-and-damage statement.

Changes between editions

  • The target period and ambition changed: BEL-NDC2 states unconditional and conditional targets of at least 35% and 40% by 2030, while BEL-NDC1 states 42% unconditional and 47% conditional by 2035, with the latter targets expressed against the 1990 base-year level and including land use. (BEL-NDC2, BEL-NDC1)
  • The later document adds explicit 2035 absolute-reduction equivalents and conditions for its conditional target, including ecosystem sink maintenance, carbon-market access, sanctions relief and external support; these formulations are not repeated in BEL-NDC2. (BEL-NDC2, BEL-NDC1)
  • The later document reports a 2035 sustainable-development strategy in implementation and plans to finalize and approve adaptation and low-emissions strategies, while the earlier NDC reports climate-policy improvement, a Paris Agreement action plan in implementation, and a prospective adaptation plan stated for 2022. The earlier document’s proposed 2022 plan is not repeated in the later findings. (BEL-NDC2, BEL-NDC1)
  • The laws listed as climate-related differ: BEL-NDC2 names hydrometeorological-activities legislation, while BEL-NDC1 names waste-management legislation; both identify environmental protection, air protection, renewable energy and energy-saving laws. BEL-NDC1 also adds emissions regulation under a 2021 resolution and periodically updated implementation plans. (BEL-NDC2, BEL-NDC1)
  • The LULUCF statements develop from inclusion in the earlier NDC despite methodological uncertainty and ongoing source-and-sink identification to a later reported 2023 sink share and emissions-and-sinks balance. (BEL-NDC2, BEL-NDC1)

Document comparison & edition notes

By document

  • BEL-NDC2 Reports climate policy focused on sustainable development and lower energy and carbon intensity, including an almost threefold carbon-intensity decline from 1995 to 2018; identifies limited capacity for additional low-carbon investment and no explicit just-transition or fossil-fuel phase-down measure.
  • BEL-NDC1 Describes a conditional 2035 economy-wide target, intended low-emission development balanced with economic resilience and food security, economic co-benefits considered, and ongoing policies to reduce fossil-fuel consumption. No specific just-transition programme or economic-restructuring measure is identified.

Changes between editions

  • BEL-NDC1 adds a stated ongoing policy to reduce fossil-fuel consumption through low-carbon energy and related measures; BEL-NDC2 reported no explicit fossil-fuel phase-down or transition measure. BEL-NDC1 also states an intended low-emission development model balanced with economic resilience and food security, and describes conditional industrial-modernization and energy-intensity outcomes; these statements are not repeated in BEL-NDC2. Neither edition identifies a specific just-transition programme. (BEL-NDC2, BEL-NDC1)
